title: Berlin Ghost Stations: Quick Summary
items: **Fifteen underground stations closed on 13 August 1961.** Five were on the U6, six on the U8 and four in the north–south S-Bahn tunnel. Above-ground Bornholmer Straße adds one more: 16 closed stations in this guide.
**The trains kept running without stopping at the closed platforms.** West Berlin passengers passed guarded stations beneath East Berlin. Berliners called them Geisterbahnhöfe, ghost stations.

**Friedrichstraße was the exception.** Passengers could change between western U-Bahn and S-Bahn services without border checks in a separate transfer area. Entering East Berlin required border controls. The Tränenpalast next door explains that crossing.

**Fifteen of the sixteen are working stations today.** These include Alexanderplatz, Naturkundemuseum and Heinrich-Heine-Straße. At Stadtmitte, only the U6 platform was sealed during the division; the U2 platform stayed open.

**Start at Nordbahnhof.** Its mezzanine holds a free permanent exhibition on the border and ghost stations, open during normal S-Bahn hours. Visit it, then walk to the Berlin Wall Memorial on Bernauer Straße.

**Französische Straße is closed again.** Its last U6 trains called on 3 December 2020. The new Unter den Linden interchange opened the next day. Potsdamer Platz, the last Cold War ghost station to reopen, returned to service on 1 March 1992.
